title: Jonathan Nichols and the Dancing Doughboys
summary: Green names his last protege Jonathan Nichols, who was Pete Nugent's protege, and Nugent's This Is the Army choreography team.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Who was John -- Jonathan Nichols a protege of?
Pete Nugent, of Peaches and Duke. See, that's the Dancing Doughboys.
Chuck, who were the Dancing Doughboys?
Well, they were the choreographers of "This is the Army." It consisted of Pete Nugent, (unintelligible) Lee, and the now Timmy Rodgers.
That was something that was done during World War II -- the show during World War II?

Yes. It was. It was a star touring, you know. It played in almost of the bases, wherever they were at, you know. Extra services they got, see, because Uncle Sam was -- you know, he's never penalized, you know.
